misconception.description: reporting the total received divided by the amount invested, which is the money multiple and counts the original stake as though it were profit

worked_example.text: A shop spends EUR 50,000 refitting itself and the refit brings in EUR 65,000 of extra gross profit over its life.
worked_example.solution: The gain is 65,000 - 50,000 = EUR 15,000. ROI = 15,000 / 50,000 = 0.3, a return of 30% on the money invested.

problem.text: A company invests EUR 400,000 in a project and receives EUR 500,000 back in total over the project's life. What is the return on investment?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: the money multiple, which treats the returned stake as profit
dividing the gain by the total received instead of by the amount put in

hints: The EUR 500,000 includes the EUR 400,000 the company put in. Separate the money returned from the money gained before dividing anything.
Return on investment is a return on the amount at risk, so the denominator is what was invested, never what came back.
Divide the gain by the investment and read the result as a percentage of the money committed.
worked_solution: Step 1: separate the stake from the gain. Of the EUR 500,000 received, EUR 400,000 is the company's own money coming home, so the gain is 500,000 - 400,000 = EUR 100,000. Step 2: divide the gain by what was invested: 100,000 / 400,000 = 0.25, a return of 25%. Reporting 500,000 / 400,000 = 125% would describe the same project as five times better than it is, because it counts the returned stake as profit. Dividing by the EUR 500,000 received instead would give 20%, which measures the gain as a share of the proceeds rather than of the risk taken.

near_transfer.text: The same project, returning EUR 500,000 on an investment of EUR 400,000, takes two years to complete. What is the simple average return per year?

distractors.note: reporting the whole-life return as though it were annual
multiplying by the years instead of dividing by them

far_transfer.text: A marketing campaign costs EUR 40,000 to run and generates EUR 100,000 of gross profit. What is the return on investment?

distractors.note: the money multiple rather than the return
the gain as a share of the profit generated rather than of the money spent
